learningObjectives.title: Immigration, intolerance and the Red Scare

questions.q: In the 1910s-1920s the USA was called a 'nation of contrasts' because:
options: Great wealth and opportunity existed alongside poverty and intolerance
questions.explain: Prosperity for some coexisted with discrimination and hardship for others.

questions.q: The 'Red Scare' of around 1919-1920 was a fear of:
questions.explain: Fear of communism led to suspicion of immigrants and radicals.

questions.q: The 1920s saw a revival of which racist organisation?
questions.explain: The KKK revived, targeting African Americans, immigrants and others.

questions.q: US immigration quotas introduced in the 1920s aimed to:
options: Restrict immigration, especially from southern and eastern Europe
questions.explain: Laws such as the 1924 Act sharply limited immigration by national origin.

questions.q: The economic boom of the 1920s was driven partly by:
options: Mass production (e.g. the assembly line) and new consumer goods
questions.explain: Techniques pioneered by Ford made goods cheaper and more available.

options: Mass-producing cars on the assembly line
questions.explain: Ford's assembly line made the Model T affordable, boosting the economy.

questions.q: Buying goods 'on credit' (hire purchase) in the 1920s:
options: Let people buy consumer goods and fuelled the boom
questions.explain: Credit allowed more consumption but also increased financial risk.
Prohibition outlawed alcohol, but led to bootlegging and organised crime.

questions.q: A major consequence of Prohibition was:
options: The growth of organised crime and gangsters
questions.explain: Illegal alcohol enriched gangsters such as Al Capone.

questions.q: Independent young women of the 1920s who challenged traditional roles were known as:
questions.explain: 'Flappers' symbolised changing attitudes and greater freedom for some women.

questions.q: Entertainment in the 1920s was transformed by:
questions.explain: Mass entertainment (movies, jazz, radio) shaped 1920s popular culture.

questions.q: Not everyone shared in the 1920s boom; those who often missed out included:
questions.explain: Agriculture struggled and discrimination excluded many from prosperity.

questions.q: The 1920s trial that highlighted prejudice against immigrants and radicals involved:
questions.explain: The controversial trial and execution of two Italian anarchists exposed prejudice.

questions.q: The 1920s boom was built on unstable foundations such as:
options: Over-production and buying shares on credit
questions.explain: These weaknesses helped cause the 1929 Wall Street Crash.

questions.q: Prohibition is often judged a failure because it:
options: Was widely ignored and boosted organised crime
questions.explain: Widespread illegal drinking and gangsterism led to its repeal in 1933.

questions.q: Attitudes to immigration hardened in the 1920s partly because of:
options: Fear of communism, job competition and prejudice
questions.explain: Economic and social fears drove restriction and intolerance.
